responses:
**Diagnosis:** Both prior attempts tied *exactly* (651.182292). Attempt 1 tied because plain Dijkstra returned the committed route (local search already made it optimal). Attempt 2 fixed candidate generation with a penalized alternate, but its enumeration was **all-or-nothing**: it only entered the joint `product` enumeration when *every* dst had a distinct alternate and `|dsts| ≤ 5`. If even one dst lacks a distinct alternate (or |dsts| > 5), it silently fell back to the default assignment — likely a no-op on most configs. The mechanism itself (splitting partitions across two routes to reduce the per-partition union cost) was never actually exercised on the mixed cases.

**Fix:** replace the all-or-nothing joint enumeration with **greedy coordinate descent over dsts**: each dst with alternates independently evaluates its split options against the current global assignment, adopts only strictly-improving choices, and sweeps until convergence (bounded). This handles subsets of dsts with alternates, small split counts, and large dst counts — while still covering everything the joint enumeration covered when all dsts have alternates. The all-on-best default is always evaluated first, so no regression; the penalized-Dijkstra alternate generator (the one part of attempt 2 that worked) is kept.

**Reasoning:** This keeps the strategy's exact gain mechanism (partition-split routing across top-2 route structures, partition-aware cost simulation, no new search beyond one penalized Dijkstra per dst) but repairs the failure mode that made both prior attempts exact ties: the joint enumeration required *every* dst to have a distinct alternate, so on configs where only some dsts have alternates (or |dsts| > 5), the code fell straight to the default and the mechanism never ran. Greedy coordinate descent operates per-dst against the evolving global assignment, exercising splits in the mixed cases the joint enumeration skipped, covers a superset of single-dst improvements (and the all-on-r1 option), and terminates in at most |dsts|+1 sweeps of O(|dsts|·P·path-len) work each — negligible compute. The default assignment is the starting point and adoption is strictly-improvement-only, so the simulated cost can never regress; all committed hops are verified directed edges of `h`/`W`, and the Dijkstra fallback for unroutable dsts is untouched.
